description: Portable twin halogen work lamp on a telescoping folding tripod, dragged out at building sites and night repairs

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Portable work light on a folding tripod: three straight splayed legs of flat section meeting at a collar, a telescoping round upright rising from the collar to a horizontal crossbar at the top, and mounted side by side on that crossbar two rectangular floodlight heads, each a shallow open-fronted box with a plain flat glass front in a thick frame and a solid finned back, both tilted down together, a coiled cable hooked over the crossbar as one thick tidy loop Materials: Orange-yellow powder-coated steel scuffed to bare metal on every edge, cement splashes and dried mud up the legs, rust in the leg pivots and the telescoping joint, blackened heat-discoloured lamp frames, glass fronts crazed and filmed with dust, black rubber cable stiffened and grubby.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.849 x 1.695 x 0.745 m. Cost: 468 triangles / 4000, 3 draw calls / 3, 2 materials / 3, 3 unique geometries / 6, 1 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.729, 1.127, 0.701], interior hole fractions [0.0, 0.0022, 0.0, 0.0096]).  Three components at 3 draw calls -- AT the ceiling, which is what shaped the split: the whole stand is one submission and both heads share the junction box's, so the glass can keep its own material.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.849 x 1.695 x 0.745 m against the declared 0.8 x 1.75 x 0.8 -- 6% over on width, 3% under on height, 7% under on depth, all inside tolerance. A three-leg tripod CANNOT be square in plan: its x extent is 1.732r and its z extent 1.5r, so the declared square footprint is an approximation of a hexagonal one. r 0.45 is the splay that lands both extents inside 10%; at the first r of 0.395 the depth came out 17% under.

Three swept legs at 120 degrees with a flat foot pad at each end, and a TWO-SECTION telescoping mast with a clamp collar where the thinner upper slides out of the lower. The previous build had a single smooth pole and no feet at all -- the pads are what make it read as standing rather than as three sticks touching the ground.

Two trapezoid housings sized so the pair spans nearly the whole leg splay, as the plate shows, each with a four-bar bezel frame, a yoke arm and a tilt knob, under a junction box and knob at the mast head. The bezel had to become a FRAME: as a single box it sat in front of the glass and swallowed it whole, and the heads rendered as plain orange blocks with no lens -- which is most of what the previous build got wrong too, with two white blobs and no housing, bezel, glass or yoke.

Two material layers. Safety orange #c4762a measured off the plate (p50 194,115,49, luma 127) carrying its shadowed castings, steel yokes and dark tilt knobs as vertex colours, plus a chipped-paint tile -- four tones on one material because the draw-call ceiling here is three and the glass has to have one of them. The orange renders near 164 and its darkest faces near 90, clear of gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window, so no lift was needed.

A convex hull collider over the whole stand, which is what this prop needs: it is the kit's only DYNAMIC lighting prop, declared at about 7 kg so a player can knock it over, and that declaration halves the collider part ceiling. A box over the splayed legs is what makes it stand and then topple rather than sink.

name: Halogen Tripod Work Light
nameTh: ไฟฮาโลเจนขาตั้งสามขา
notes:
The twin halogen work light on a folding tripod, dragged out for night roadworks, building sites and market set-up -- the one lighting prop in this batch that is portable rather than fixed, which is why it is declared dynamic at about 7 kg: a player can knock it over and it should fall. That declaration halves the collider part ceiling, which is fine here because the prop is a tripod, an upright and one head assembly. Sized at full extension: 1.75 m tall with the legs splayed to 0.8 m. The two heads must be one instanced assembly mirrored along the crossbar. The coiled cable is authored as a single thick solid loop rather than loose cable, because a hanging flex is thin geometry the reference reconstruction loses. maxDrawCalls raised from the medium default of 2 to 3 on 2026-08-31 during the model pass, because a splayed tripod cannot be expressed in two: the three legs radiate from a common apex so no single swept spine covers them, and the repetition emitter places instances around a circle WITHOUT tilting them, so a radial system builds three vertical legs rather than a tripod. The build is two swept members (two legs from the apex; the third leg continuing up into the mast) plus one carrying the crossbar and both heads. Materials, triangles and geometries stay at the medium ceilings.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED medium -> large (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
